# Functional Testing — Associate-Level Interview Cheatsheet

---

## 1\. What is Functional Testing?

Testing that verifies **what the system does** — each function/feature is checked against functional requirements (inputs → expected outputs), without concern for internal code structure (black-box approach).

**Contrast with Non-Functional Testing:** Non-functional testing checks *how* the system performs — performance, security, usability, scalability — not *what* it does.

| Functional Testing | Non-Functional Testing |
| :---- | :---- |
| Validates features/business requirements | Validates quality attributes |
| Black-box | Can be black/white/grey box |
| Examples: Unit, Integration, System, UAT | Examples: Load, Stress, Security, Usability |

---

## 2\. Software Testing Life Cycle (STLC)

```
Requirement Analysis → Test Planning → Test Case Development →
Test Environment Setup → Test Execution → Test Cycle Closure
```

| Phase | Key Activity |
| :---- | :---- |
| Requirement Analysis | Understand what to test; identify testable requirements |
| Test Planning | Define scope, strategy, resources, schedule, tools (Test Plan doc) |
| Test Case Development | Write test cases, test data, RTM (Requirement Traceability Matrix) |
| Environment Setup | Configure test environment (server, DB, test data) |
| Test Execution | Execute test cases, log defects |
| Test Cycle Closure | Test summary report, closure metrics, lessons learned |

**RTM (Requirement Traceability Matrix):** Maps each requirement to its corresponding test case(s) — ensures full coverage, no requirement is left untested.

---

## 3\. SDLC vs STLC

| SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) | STLC (Software Testing Life Cycle) |
| :---- | :---- |
| Requirement → Design → Development → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance | Requirement Analysis → Planning → Case Design → Env Setup → Execution → Closure |
| Focus: building the product | Focus: validating the product |
| Runs parallel/overlapping with STLC | Testing team's dedicated cycle |

---

## 4\. STLC vs SDLC Models (Common Models Asked)

| Model | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Waterfall | Sequential phases; testing occurs after development is complete |
| V-Model | Each dev phase has a corresponding testing phase (verification & validation) |
| Agile/Scrum | Iterative sprints; testing happens continuously within each sprint |
| Spiral | Risk-driven, iterative with repeated prototyping and testing |

---

## 5\. Levels of Testing

```
Unit Testing → Integration Testing → System Testing → Acceptance Testing (UAT)
```

| Level | Performed By | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Unit Testing | Developers | Test individual components/functions in isolation |
| Integration Testing | Developers/Testers | Test interaction between integrated modules |
| System Testing | Testers | End-to-end testing of complete, integrated system |
| Acceptance Testing (UAT) | Client/End Users | Validate system meets business needs, ready for release |

**Integration Testing Approaches:**

- **Big Bang** — integrate all modules at once, test as a whole  
- **Top-Down** — test from top-level modules downward, using stubs for lower modules  
- **Bottom-Up** — test from lower-level modules upward, using drivers for upper modules  
- **Sandwich/Hybrid** — combination of top-down and bottom-up

---

## 6\. Types of Functional Testing

| Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Smoke Testing | Quick check that critical/major functionalities work — "build stability" check before deeper testing |
| Sanity Testing | Narrow, focused check on specific functionality/bug fix after minor changes |
| Regression Testing | Re-test to ensure new changes haven't broken existing functionality |
| Retesting | Re-verify a specific defect is fixed (different from regression) |
| Integration Testing | Test interaction between modules |
| System Testing | Full end-to-end test of the entire application |
| UAT (User Acceptance Testing) | Business/end-user validates against real-world scenarios |
| Interface Testing | Validate communication between systems (API/UI/DB interfaces) |
| Cross-Browser/Cross-Platform Testing | Verify functionality across browsers/devices/OS |

**Smoke vs Sanity (frequently asked):** | Smoke Testing | Sanity Testing | |---|---| | Broad and shallow | Narrow and deep | | Done on a fresh build | Done after minor code fix/change | | Verifies build stability | Verifies specific bug fix / functionality | | Usually scripted | Usually unscripted |

**Retesting vs Regression Testing:** | Retesting | Regression Testing | |---|---| | Confirms a specific defect is fixed | Confirms existing features still work after changes | | Planned, defect-specific | Broader scope, not necessarily defect-specific | | Cannot be automated (verifies exact defect scenario) | Can be automated |

---

## 7\. Test Case Design Techniques

### Black-Box Techniques

| Technique | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Equivalence Partitioning (EP) | Divide input data into valid/invalid partitions; test one value per partition |
| Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) | Test at boundaries of input ranges (min, min+1, max, max-1) |
| Decision Table Testing | Test combinations of inputs/conditions and their resulting actions |
| State Transition Testing | Test system behavior across different states (e.g., login attempts, order status) |
| Use Case Testing | Derive test cases from user use case scenarios |
| Error Guessing | Tester's experience-based guessing of likely defect areas |

**Example — BVA:** For an age field accepting 18–60: Test values: 17 (invalid), 18 (valid boundary), 19, 59, 60 (valid boundary), 61 (invalid)

### White-Box Techniques (Good to know, dev-oriented)

| Technique | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Statement Coverage | Every line of code executed at least once |
| Branch/Decision Coverage | Every branch (if/else) executed at least once |
| Path Coverage | Every possible path through code executed |
| Condition Coverage | Every boolean sub-expression evaluated true/false |

### Experience-Based

- **Exploratory Testing** — simultaneous learning, test design, and execution without predefined scripts.  
- **Ad-hoc Testing** — informal, unstructured testing without any plan/documentation.

---

## 8\. Test Case & Test Plan Structure

**Test Case Components:**

```
Test Case ID | Test Scenario | Description | Preconditions |
Test Steps | Test Data | Expected Result | Actual Result | Status (Pass/Fail) | Priority
```

**Test Plan Components:**

```
Scope | Objectives | Test Strategy | Test Environment | Entry/Exit Criteria |
Resources & Roles | Schedule | Risk & Mitigation | Deliverables
```

**Entry Criteria:** Conditions that must be met before testing starts (e.g., test environment ready, requirements finalized, build deployed).

**Exit Criteria:** Conditions that must be met before testing is considered complete (e.g., all critical test cases executed, defect count below threshold).

---

## 9\. Defect/Bug Life Cycle

```
New → Assigned → Open → Fixed → Retest → Verified → Closed
                    ↓
                 Reopened (if issue persists)
                    ↓
                Rejected / Deferred / Duplicate (alternate paths)
```

![][image1]

| Status | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| New | Defect logged, not yet reviewed |
| Assigned | Assigned to a developer |
| Open | Developer starts working |
| Fixed | Developer fixes and marks resolved |
| Retest | Tester re-verifies the fix |
| Verified | Fix confirmed working |
| Closed | Defect resolved and confirmed closed |
| Reopened | Issue still exists after "fix" |
| Rejected | Not a valid defect (as designed/duplicate) |
| Deferred | Fix postponed to a later release |
| Duplicate | Same as an already-logged defect |

**Defect Report Fields:** Defect ID, Title/Summary, Description, Steps to Reproduce, Expected vs Actual Result, Severity, Priority, Environment, Screenshots/Logs, Status.

**Severity vs Priority (VERY frequently asked):** | Severity | Priority | |---|---| | Impact of the defect on the application | Urgency of fixing the defect | | Decided by Tester | Decided by Business/Project Manager (usually) | | Example: App crash \= High Severity | Example: Logo color wrong \= Low Severity, but High Priority if it's for a big client demo tomorrow |

**Severity Levels:** Critical, High, Medium, Low **Priority Levels:** High, Medium, Low

**Classic example combos:**

- High Severity \+ High Priority → App crashes on login  
- High Severity \+ Low Priority → A rarely-used report feature crashes  
- Low Severity \+ High Priority → Company logo/spelling mistake on homepage  
- Low Severity \+ Low Priority → Minor UI misalignment on an internal admin page

---

## 10\. Verification vs Validation

| Verification | Validation |
| :---- | :---- |
| "Are we building the product right?" | "Are we building the right product?" |
| Static technique (reviews, walkthroughs, inspections) | Dynamic technique (actual execution/testing) |
| Done without executing code | Done by executing code |
| Example: Requirement/document review | Example: Executing test cases |

---

## 11\. Static vs Dynamic Testing

| Static Testing | Dynamic Testing |
| :---- | :---- |
| Done without executing the code | Done by executing the code |
| Reviews, walkthroughs, inspections, static analysis tools | Unit, integration, system, acceptance testing |
| Finds issues early (requirements/design phase) | Finds issues during/after code execution |

---

## 12\. Test Design & Review Types

| Review Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Informal Review | Quick, no formal documented process |
| Walkthrough | Author leads peers through the document |
| Technical Review | Peer experts evaluate technical correctness |
| Inspection | Most formal; uses defined roles, checklists, metrics |

---

## 13\. Agile Testing Concepts

- **Sprint** — a fixed time-box (usually 1–4 weeks) in which a set of work is completed.  
- **Scrum roles** — Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team (includes testers).  
- **Daily Standup** — short daily sync meeting.  
- **Sprint Planning / Review / Retrospective** — key Scrum ceremonies.  
- **User Story** — a feature described from an end-user perspective; often has **Acceptance Criteria** that define "done."  
- **Definition of Done (DoD)** — checklist of what must be true for a story to be considered complete (includes testing).  
- **Shift-Left Testing** — testing early in the SDLC (during requirements/design) instead of only after development, to catch defects sooner.  
- **BDD (Behavior Driven Development)** — uses Given-When-Then (Gherkin) syntax to define behavior collaboratively (e.g., Cucumber).

```
Feature: Login
  Scenario: Successful login with valid credentials
    Given the user is on the login page
    When the user enters valid username and password
    Then the user should be redirected to the dashboard
```

---

## 14\. Test Metrics (Often Asked)

| Metric | Formula/Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Defect Density | Number of defects / size of module (e.g., per KLOC) |
| Defect Leakage | Defects found in UAT / production ÷ Total defects found (measures escaped defects) |
| Test Coverage | (Requirements tested / Total requirements) × 100 |
| Defect Rejection Ratio | Rejected defects / Total defects reported |
| Pass Percentage | (Passed test cases / Total executed test cases) × 100 |

---

## 15\. Types of Non-Functional Testing (Good to Know for Context)

| Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Performance Testing | System behavior under expected load |
| Load Testing | Behavior under expected concurrent user load |
| Stress Testing | Behavior beyond normal capacity, till breaking point |
| Scalability Testing | Ability to scale up/down with load |
| Usability Testing | Ease of use / user experience |
| Security Testing | Vulnerabilities, authentication, data protection |
| Compatibility Testing | Across browsers, devices, OS versions |
| Recovery Testing | System's ability to recover from crashes/failures |

---

## 16\. Manual vs Automation Testing

| Manual Testing | Automation Testing |
| :---- | :---- |
| Human executes test cases | Scripts/tools execute test cases |
| Good for exploratory, usability, ad-hoc testing | Good for repetitive, regression, data-driven testing |
| Slower, more error-prone for repetitive tasks | Faster, consistent, reusable |
| No coding needed | Requires scripting/tool knowledge (Selenium, etc.) |

**When NOT to automate:** One-time tests, frequently changing UI, exploratory/usability testing, tests with very low ROI.

---

## 17\. Test Environment & Test Data Concepts

- **Test Data** — the actual input values used to execute test cases (valid, invalid, boundary, edge cases).  
- **Test Environment** — hardware/software setup (server, DB, browser, network) where testing is executed; should closely mirror production.  
- **Test Bed** — combination of hardware and software the test environment is built on.  
- **Sandbox Environment** — isolated environment used for testing without affecting live/production data.

---

## 18\. Common Testing Documents

| Document | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| BRD (Business Requirement Document) | High-level business needs |
| FRD/FSD (Functional/Functional Spec Document) | Detailed functional requirements |
| Test Plan | Overall testing approach/strategy |
| Test Case Document | Detailed steps to validate functionality |
| RTM (Requirement Traceability Matrix) | Maps requirements to test cases |
| Defect Report | Documents found bugs |
| Test Summary Report | Final report post test execution (pass/fail stats, open defects, etc.) |

## 19\. Quick-Fire Q\&A (Rapid Revision)

**Q: What is the difference between Functional and Structural (White-Box) testing?** A: Functional testing validates behavior against requirements without knowledge of code (black-box); structural testing validates internal code paths/logic (white-box).

**Q: What's the difference between Smoke and Regression testing?** A: Smoke testing checks basic build stability before deeper testing begins; regression testing re-checks existing functionality after changes to ensure nothing broke.

**Q: What is a Test Scenario vs a Test Case?** A: A test scenario is a high-level "what to test" statement (e.g., "verify login functionality"); a test case is the detailed step-by-step "how to test it," with specific data and expected results.

**Q: Can Severity be High and Priority be Low?** A: Yes — e.g., a crash in a rarely-used feature is high severity (breaks functionality) but might be low priority (few users affected, can wait for the next release).

**Q: What is Boundary Value Analysis?** A: A test design technique focused on values at the edges of valid input ranges, since defects often occur at boundaries (min, min-1, max, max+1).

**Q: What's the difference between Alpha and Beta Testing?** A: Alpha testing is done in-house by the internal team before release; beta testing is done by a limited set of real, external end-users in a real environment before public release.

**Q: What is Exploratory Testing?** A: Unscripted testing where the tester simultaneously learns the app, designs tests, and executes them — relies on tester's intuition and experience, common in Agile.

**Q: What's the difference between Test Strategy and Test Plan?** A: Test Strategy is a high-level, project-independent document defining the overall testing approach (organization-level); Test Plan is a project-specific document detailing scope, schedule, resources for that particular project.

**Q: What is a false positive / false negative in testing?** A: False positive — a test reports a failure/defect when none actually exists (script/environment issue). False negative — a test reports a pass when there actually is a defect (test didn't catch a real bug).

**Q: How do you prioritize test cases when time is limited?** A: Prioritize based on business-critical functionality, high-risk areas, frequently used features, and areas with historically high defect density.
